description: Fig. 4 is a 3 × 3 composite of TEM bright-field micrographs; every panel carries a SAED inset in its upper-right corner and a 500 nm scale bar in its lower-right corner. Panels are labelled by alloy and phase: (a) 4Al γ, (b) 6Al γ, (c) 6Al α, (d) 8Al γ, (e) 8Al γ, (f) 8Al α, (g) 10Al γ, (h) 10Al α, (i) 10Al α, so the same aluminium level is imaged in both austenite and ferrite. (a) and (d) show dark, irregular dislocation cell-block walls in austenite; (b) shows elongated banded dark contrast in 6Al austenite. (e) is 8Al austenite whose inset marks an extra spot annotated (111)M_T, consistent with deformation twinning. (g) shows dense, tangled, largely planar dislocation lines in 10Al austenite crossed by white dashed traces. The ferrite panels (c) and (f) display straight slip-band structures with white dashed traces labelled by plane indices; (h) and (i) contain long straight dislocations marked by red dashed lines labelled 'Screw', and (i) also carries a magenta 'Mixed' annotation. Inset reflections are indexed (002)/(111)/(111) along [110]γ for austenite and (101)/(011)/(110) for ferrite. The group argues that austenite deforms by cell blocks plus minor twinning, whereas ferrite deforms by pronounced planar slip, with 10Al ferrite activating only a few long straight screw dislocations.

subfigures.description: 4Al γ bright-field TEM: diffuse dark dislocation cell-block walls in an austenite matrix, no long-range banding. SAED inset indexed (002), (111), (111) with zone axis [110]γ; 500 nm scale bar.
6Al γ bright-field TEM: elongated, aligned dark banded contrast (dense dislocation bands) running across the field. SAED inset indexed (002), (111), (111), zone axis [110]γ; 500 nm scale bar.

6Al α ferrite bright-field TEM: straight parallel slip-band contrast crossed by two white dashed traces labelled with plane indices. SAED inset indexed (101), (011), (110), zone axis [111]α; 500 nm scale bar.
8Al γ bright-field TEM: mottled, tangled dislocation cell network typical of cell-block structure in austenite. SAED inset indexed (111), (002), (111), zone axis [110]γ; 500 nm scale bar.

8Al γ bright-field TEM: banded dislocation structure with a white arrowed line and dashed trace; the SAED inset marks an extra reflection annotated (111)M_T inside the (002)/(111)/(111) pattern along [110]γ, indicating deformation twins. 500 nm scale bar.

8Al α ferrite bright-field TEM: pronounced long straight slip bands, more distinctly planar than in (c), crossed by white dashed index traces. SAED inset indexed (101), (011), (110), zone axis [111]α; 500 nm scale bar.

10Al γ bright-field TEM: very dense, mostly straight and parallel dislocation lines traversing the whole field, with white dashed traces and index labels; no cell walls. SAED inset indexed (111), (002), (111), zone axis [110]γ; 500 nm scale bar.

10Al α ferrite bright-field TEM: comparatively clean matrix containing a few long straight dislocations highlighted by a red dashed line labelled 'Screw', plus a white dashed trace with an index label. SAED inset indexed (101), (011), (110); 500 nm scale bar.

10Al α ferrite bright-field TEM: mixed dislocation configuration — long straight red-dashed lines each annotated 'Screw' together with a magenta 'Mixed' annotation and white dashed index traces. SAED inset indexed (011), (211), (200); 500 nm scale bar.

observations.observation: The figure is a 3 × 3 array of TEM bright-field micrographs, each with an upper-right SAED inset and a 500 nm scale bar in the lower-right corner.
Panel labels printed on the images are (a) 4Al γ, (b) 6Al γ, (c) 6Al α, (d) 8Al γ, (e) 8Al γ, (f) 8Al α, (g) 10Al γ, (h) 10Al α and (i) 10Al α.

Austenite panels (a) and (d) show irregular dark dislocation cell-block walls, whereas (b) shows elongated aligned dislocation bands and (g) shows dense straight planar dislocation lines rather than cells.
The SAED inset of panel (e) contains an extra reflection annotated (111)M_T in addition to the (002)/(111)/(111) austenite spots, indicating deformation twinning in 8Al austenite.

Ferrite panels (h) and (i) mark long straight dislocations with red dashed lines labelled 'Screw', and (i) additionally carries a magenta 'Mixed' label; ferrite panels (c) and (f) show straight slip-band structures without these 'Screw' annotations.

SAED insets of the austenite panels are indexed (002), (111), (111) about zone axis [110]γ; those of the ferrite panels are indexed (101), (011), (110) in (c), (f) and (h), and (011), (211), (200) in (i).
The caption assigns the deformation microstructures to 4Al (a), 6Al (b, c), 8Al (d–f) and 10Al (g–i) steels after tensile testing, with (a, b, d, e, g) austenite and (c, f, h, i) ferrite.
The citing text states that the austenite deformation microstructure is characterized by dislocation cell blocks regardless of aluminium content, as shown in Fig. 4(a, b, d).
The citing text states that a small number of deformation twins are observed in 8Al steel (Fig. 4(e)), associated with stress localization.
Because of the plastic instability of the 10Al steel, the citing text says the 10Al microstructures of Fig. 4(g–i) were taken after fracture at ~3 % engineering strain.

The citing text states that ferrite dislocations show distinct planar slip (Fig. 4(c–f, h, i)), more pronounced in 8Al than 6Al, and that only a few long straight dislocations identified as screw dislocations are activated in the 10Al ferrite matrix.

The citing text lists ferrite as Fig. 4(c–f, h, i) while the caption assigns (d) and (e) to austenite; the two descriptions of panel membership disagree, and the printed panel labels on the images read (d) 8Al γ and (e) 8Al γ.
